Diego / team —

Attached is a concise calc (marginal-vs-blend-calcs.csv) with the worked example for ScaleHealth’s six-month ramp. Summary:

- Assumptions: list per-token = $0.000012 per token (baseline).
- Bands used: 0–150M @ 2% off, 150–250M @ 4% off, 250–500M (anchor) @ 8% off, >500M @ 12% off.

Worked example (selected months):
- Month1 (100M): marginal price -> 100M * (0.000012 * 0.98) = $1,176; blended effective = same here because only first band used.
- Month3 (260M): marginal invoice = (150M*0.000012*0.98) + (110M*0.000012*0.96) = $2,891; blended effective price across 260M = $2,891 / 260M = $0.00001112 per token (roughly 7.3% effective discount vs list).
- Steady state (300M): marginal invoice structure saves ~6–8% vs a single blended discount that would need to be set conservatively to cover tail months.

Implications:
- Marginal is cleaner from a unit economics perspective (accurately credits incremental volume), and allows us to keep anchor bands tight without over-discounting early months.
- Blended invoices are easier for clients to forecast but tend to lock in a higher effective discount when large months hit, which hurts us on months below the blended threshold.

Recommendation: present both views (we already have the blended tab) but lead with marginal as the primary billing mechanism, and offer an optional monthly blended statement on request for finance reporting purposes.

Also recommended: soft-cap policy — if a month exceeds the highest band by >20%, apply an automatic notice + buffer credits equal to 5% of overage (one-time) and bill overage at standard hosted list rate thereafter unless the account upgrades the anchor. This avoids emergency throttles and gives ScaleHealth room to normalize.

-Karthik
Director, Pricing Strategy
Redwood Inference

Samira —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for looping procurement. We took your ramp request into account and ran both marginal and blended scenarios against your forecast (see attached calc). High-level proposal below — happy to jump on a short call to walk it through:

Proposed commercial shape (short summary):
- Anchor: 250M tokens/month (committed).
- Initial ramp band: 0–150M -> 2% off list.
- Mid band: 150–250M -> 4% off list.
- Anchor band: 250–500M -> 8% off list (this is the primary anchor we’d price to).
- Velocity band: >500M -> 12% off list.

Billing mechanics:
- Primary billing method: marginal per-token pricing (each band charged at its discounted per-token rate).
- Optional: monthly blended invoice view for finance (client-facing report only; underlying billing stays marginal).
- True-up cadence: monthly (per your request).

Guardrails / overconsumption policy:
- If monthly usage > highest band by 20%: automatic notice, one-time buffer credit calculated at 5% of the overage, and remainder billed at standard hosted list rate.
- If sustained >120% for 2 consecutive months, we’ll automatically open a capacity review and recommend anchor re-evaluation or short-term burst credits.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm the anchor and bands, we’ll draft a short exhibit + SOW and share it with your procurement/legal.
2) We’ll include the optional monthly blended statement as a reporting attachment so your finance team can forecast.
3) I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with you + procurement next week — propose Wed 12/16 at 10am PT.

If that works, I’ll start the term-sheet and loop legal for an abbreviated review.

Best,
